purpose: Teach: 除け/処方/知見/養う/備える/凶/調書/力強く

lines.speaker: saito_doctor
lines.jp: 蓮さん、虫除けスプレー、子供にも安心なもの、増えています。
lines.en: Ren, kid-safe insect repellent sprays are becoming much more available now.
lines.style: Measured and informative. Even pace, warm but clinical. A doctor sharing practical knowledge she's observed. No rush—this is reassurance in the form of fact.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 処方薬、ジェネリック、普及してきましたね。
lines.en: Generic prescription medications have become much more widespread, haven't they.
lines.style: Thoughtful, gently probing. Speaks from genuine curiosity, not uncertainty. Slow pace. Respects the doctor's expertise while thinking aloud with her.

lines.speaker: saito_doctor
lines.jp: はい。最新の医学的知見、患者さんと共有しています。
lines.en: Yes. We make it a point to share the latest medical knowledge with our patients.
lines.style: Clear and steady. Professional but not distant. Matter-of-fact delivery on 「はい」. Slight emphasis on 「患者さん」—pride in the relationship.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 家族が高齢者を養う負担、医療として、軽減策はありますか。
lines.en: Is there anything the medical system offers to lighten the burden on families caring for elderly relatives?
lines.style: Quiet and earnest. Leans slightly forward. This is a real question, not rhetorical. Careful, almost vulnerable—he's asking for someone, maybe himself.

lines.speaker: saito_doctor
lines.jp: はい。感染症に備える体制、強化されています。
lines.en: Yes. We've strengthened our systems to better prepare for infectious disease outbreaks.
lines.style: Measured response to a serious question. Slightly slower pace. Direct eye contact. Doctor-to-person rather than doctor-to-patient. Honest without being heavy.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 昔は、凶作で栄養失調、多かったんでしょうね。
lines.en: In older times, crop failures meant malnutrition was common, didn't it.
lines.style: Reflective, almost to himself. Slow pace, gentle curiosity. He's drawing a line from past to present. Not quite a question—more a thought he's sharing.

lines.speaker: saito_doctor
lines.jp: はい。診療調書、電子化、進めております。
lines.en: Yes. We're working on digitizing patient medical records across the system.
lines.style: Professional acknowledgment. Steady rhythm. Brief pause after 「はい」—she's keeping pace with where his mind is going, not just answering the surface question.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 医療従事者の力強く支える姿、頼もしいですね。
lines.en: The way healthcare workers support people so steadily—it's really reassuring.
lines.style: Warm and genuine close. Slower pace. Not performing gratitude—simply noticing something true. Slight lift on the final phrase, like he's settling something in himself.
